en: Morning dew on saluyasi leaves forms when water vapor in the air condenses into liquid water.
Beach sand in Boracay is a heterogeneous mixture of crushed coral, shells, and quartz minerals.
Iron roofs in coastal Manila rust faster because saltwater accelerates the chemical reaction between iron and oxygen.
Flowing lava from Mayon Volcano solidifies into black basalt rock as it cools, demonstrating a change of state.
Seawater in the West Philippine Sea is a homogeneous solution where salt is the solute dissolved in water.
Pumice stones from Taal Volcano float on water because their porous structure makes their overall density lower than water.
Fallen mangoes rotting on the ground undergo a chemical change as bacteria break them down into compost.
Puddles on a schoolyard in Quezon City disappear on sunny days because liquid water evaporates into an invisible gas.
Muddy water from the Pasig River after a typhoon is a suspension where solid soil particles temporarily float in water.
Magnetite sand found in the black sand beaches of Ilocos is naturally magnetic and can be attracted by a lodestone.
Coconut oil extracted from copra melts from a solid to a liquid when exposed to the hot tropical sun.
Leaves of the acacia tree turn yellow and brown in the dry season due to a chemical change breaking down chlorophyll.
